E1 West Bank settlement — UN and international reaction (19-21 Aug 2026):
- UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed "deep alarm" over reports of new illegal
  Israeli settlement outposts and tenders in the occupied West Bank. He warned that
  expanding settlements in the E1 sector would effectively "sever the connection between
  the northern and the southern West Bank", posing an "existential threat" to the two-state
  solution and the territorial integrity of Palestinian lands.
- The E1 plan includes a tender for more than 1,200 new housing units issued by the Israeli
  government this week.
- Guterres called on Israel to refrain from taking any further steps and to comply with
  relevant UN resolutions and the ICJ Advisory Opinion of 19 July 2024, which found Israel's
  occupation of the West Bank, including East Jerusalem, "unlawful".
- Leaders of France, Germany, Italy, the Netherlands, Norway and the United Kingdom issued
  a joint statement calling the Israeli government's decision to publish construction tenders
  for the E1 settlement project "unacceptable".
- (Morning brief, cross-ref: Israel's finance minister hailed the plan, saying "the
  Palestinian state is being erased".)
